displayedInputs.question:
Points \(K,\) \(L,\) \(M,\) and \(N\) lie in the plane of the square \(ABCD\) so that \(AKB,\) \(BLC,\) \(CMD,\) and \(DNA\) are equilateral triangles. If \(ABCD\) has an area of \(16,\) find the area of \(KLMN.\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

A semicircle of diameter \(1\) sits at the top of a semicircle of diameter \(2,\) as shown. The shaded area inside the smaller semicircle and outside the larger semicircle is called a lune. Determine the area of this lune.

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

Square \(ABCD\) has sides of length \(4,\) and \(M\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{CD}.\) A circle with radius \(2\) and center \(M\) intersects a circle with radius \(4\) and center \(A\) at points \(P\) and \(D.\) What is the distance from \(P\) to \(\overline{AD}?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

Rose fills each of the rectangular regions of her rectangular flower bed with a different type of flower. The lengths, in feet, of the rectangular regions in her flower bed are as shown in the figure. She plants one flower per square foot in each region. Asters cost \(\$1\) each, begonias \(\$1.50\) each, cannas \(\$2\) each, dahlias \(\$2.50\) each, and Easter lilies \(\$3\) each. What is the least possible cost, in dollars, for her garden?

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

Many television screens are rectangles that are measured by the length of their diagonals. The ratio of the horizontal length to the height in a standard television screen is \(4 : 3.\) The horizontal length of a \(27\)-inch television screen is closest, in inches, to which of the following?

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

Several figures can be made by attaching two equilateral triangles to the regular pentagon \(ABCDE\) in two of the five positions shown. How many non-congruent figures can be constructed in this way?

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

In rectangle \(ABCD,\) \(AB = 5\) and \(BC = 3.\) Points \(F\) and \(G\) are on \(\overline{CD}\) so that \(DF = 1\) and \(GC = 2.\) Lines \(AF\) and \(BG\) intersect at \(E.\) Find the area of \(\triangle AEB.\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

A regular octagon \(ABCDEFGH\) has an area of one square unit. What is the area of the rectangle \(ABEF?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)

mappings.rationale: The requested triangle area requires its perpendicular height. Parallel segments FG and AB allow a similarity calculation; alternatively, coordinate line equations locate E directly.
mappings.answerReason: FG = 5 − 1 − 2 = 2. If H is E's height above AB, similarity gives (H − 3)/H = 2/5, hence H = 5. Therefore the area is (1/2)(5)(5) = 25/2.

mappings.rationale: Decomposing the regular octagon into eight central triangles relates its area to the side length and apothem. The same quantities determine the shaded rectangle's area without computing any radicals.
mappings.answerReason: Let the octagon's side length be s and apothem be a. Its area is 8(sa/2) = 4sa = 1. Rectangle ABEF has width s and height 2a, so its area is 2sa = 1/2.
